newsitem.title: USA: AT&T sees competition hurting second half profits.
newsitem.headline: AT&T sees competition hurting second half profits.

text.p: AT&T Corp., citing competition in its key long-distance telephone business, said on Tuesday its third-quarter earnings could be as much as 10 percent below Wall Street estimates and the pressure will continue for the rest of the year.

Chairman Robert Allen said in a statement that AT&T's third-quarter results appeared to be as much as 10 percent below analysts' mean estimate of 92 cents a share and that the fourth quarter will likely fall short of the mean estimate of 89 cents a share.
Allen also said the company's earnings were being affected by its investments in local, on-line and wireless services as well as infrastucure to provide new communications and information services.
"Further, we currently believe that competitive pressures will continue for the remainder of the year, and we are intensifying our marketing efforts," Allen said in a statement.

In a separate announcement Tuesday, the company took aim at competitors with a new long-distance calling plan that would give consumers the option of a flat calling rate of 15 cents a minute at any time to anywhere in the United States.
News that New York-based AT&T, one of the most widely held stocks, expects poor second-half results was expected to send stock prices lower.

"Mother Bell has been a sacred cow until now. This type of news is going to be disquieting," said Fahnestock & Co. market analyst Alan Ackerman. "Its likely to put a lot of pressure on the stock and ruffle the feathers of many shareholders."
AT&T shares fell $3.25 to $54 in pre-opening trade after the announcement, traders said.
